newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aum guru rants at testimony of gas victims' agony.
newsitem.headline: Aum guru rants at testimony of gas victims' agony.

text.p: The doomsday cult guru accused of a 1995 Tokyo subway nerve gas attack ranted incoherently in court on Friday as witnesses told for the first time of the agony of victims of the attack.

Tsutomu Omuro, a ticket collector on Tokyo's Hibiya subway line, told Tokyo District Court how he tried to carry collapsed passengers to safety in the confusion shortly after the deadly sarin nerve gas was released inside the station where he was working.
"People were lying around the platform crying and moaning. One passenger was carrying a man who couldn't stand up. We carried him into the station office...but he later died," Omuro said.

The testimony came a day after Asahara, leader of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth) sect, told the Tokyo District Court he was not guilty of 15 of the 16 other charges levelled against him and blamed his followers for the gassing.

Throughout Friday's proceedings the long-bearded guru, dressed in a dark-blue prison track suit, interrupted testimony by waving his right hand furiously and interjecting an assortment of nonsensical outbursts in Japanese and English.
"I am Shoko Asahara," the cult leader exclaimed sonorously in English, later declaring: "I will go to Heaven."
Asahara faces death by hanging if found guilty of murder.
